Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Summary 2 Terms 3 Actions 3.1 All Players: 3.2 Captain: 3.3 First Mate: 3.4 Cabin Boy: 3.5 Governor: 4 Vote Cards 4.1 Attack 4.2 Brawl 4.3 Mutiny 5 Getting Marooned 6 Rowboats 7 Ending and Winning the Game 8 Event Cards 8.1 Helpful Cards (6) 8.2 Hurtful Cards (6) 8.3 Treasure Maps (3) 8.4 Starred Cards (3 added into each game at random) 8.5 Game Ender (1) Summary Players will be divided into teams evenly (British and French), if there are an odd number of players, there will be one lone Dutch player. Either way, the team you are on is secret, and you may not reveal your team to the other players After this, players are randomly distributed to the two boats. To finish setup, the captain of each ship decides which nationality's hold the first treasure for their ship starts at The winner is the team that has the most chests in their team's holds when the Spanish Armada event card is revealed. The Dutch team only wins if the British and French teams are tied at the end of the game. If there is no Dutch team, then the Spanish Armada is removed and event deck is shuffled and the game continues until it is no longer tied. Terms * Captain: The person at the front of either ship. * First Mate: The person on the second space of either ship. * Cabin Boy: The last person on the ship. This may be the first mate or the captain if alone. * Governor: This is the first person in the line on Tortuga. Actions On your turn there are a number of actions you can perform and they depend on where your character is located. NOTE: In 2-player games, each player gets 2 actions per turn. All Players: * View 2 Event Cards: Secretly view the front of any 2 of the 5 face-down Event cards * Reveal 1 Event Card: Reveal any 1 of the event cards. Show this card to all players and resolve the consequences listed on the card. Replace the revealed card with the top card from the event deck face-down * Force another player to reveal one of two event cards: Choose any other player and then select any 2 of the event cards. The player you chose selects either of those 2 event cards, reveals it to all players, and resolves it * Move: Move your pawn from either ship or Tortuga to an adjoining rowboat. Or, move your pawn from a rowboat to the back of the line on Tortuga or to the back of the line on the adjoining ship Captain: * Call for an Attack: Successful attacks let you take treasure from the Spanish Galleon. If the Spanish Galleon is out of treasure, successful attacks let you take treasure from the other pirate ship. See “Vote Cards” section for details * Maroon a player: Maroon any other pawn on your ship to Tortuga First Mate: * Call for a Mutiny: Successful mutinies maroon your captain to Tortuga. See “Vote Cards” section for details Cabin Boy: * Move a Treasure: Move 1 treasure token already on your ship from the British treasure hold to the French treasure hold, or vice versa Governor: * Call for a Brawl: Brawls move the 2 pieces of treasure already on Tortuga to one or both treasure areas on Tortuga. See “Vote Cards” section for details Vote Cards Attacks, Mutinies, and Brawls are all types of votes. When a vote is called for, all players participating in the vote will put 1 of their vote cards into the middle. For each type of vote, the top vote card from the vote deck is also added. [Rating: 2/10] This game sounds awesome and looks great. The game mechanics are fairly awful unless you make house rules.

[Rating: 2/10] Without the odd Dutchman, I am dubious that any player could remain hidden which might render the roles wrote.

[Rating: 2/10] Nice components,  but way too much take that and the action selection is simple and quite boring.  The memory aspect is rather annoying as well.  I'm going to have to maroon this game.

[Rating: 2/10] Very disappointed in this game.  The "hidden roles" are anything but, by your second or third turn it will be painfully obvious who belongs to either the British or the French.  And I don't care who the Dutch player is, because that player's win condition is so laughably hard to line up that there's no reason to speculate who is that role.  The actions related to looking at/playing/forcing others to play/etc are tactical, which isn't necessarily bad, but watching your player piece get tossed around or marooned or losing turns or whatever does not feel justified 90% of the time. [Rating: 2/10] If you played this as a group it might be okay. It was not good as a two player game

[Rating: 2/10] Played on BGA asynchronous, which is a bad start.  Theme is fun, but none of the choices are remotely interesting.

[Rating: 3/10] Severely disappointed. There is very little a team can do to come back, other than randomly draw cards and hope for lucky draws. Captains can do far too much and other ship mates can be kicked off at the whim of the captain. Nice that it is short, but not so short that I ever feel the need to play again.  Nice components. i am hoping someone comes up with better house rules/variants to make this actually playable or fun.

[Rating: 3/10] Game looks great on the table, and they did well integrating the pirate theme throughout the graphic design and mechanics. Main issue is that there are too many mechanics that force randomness, limiting player's abilities to ascertain other player's nationalities, thus further limiting meaningful decisions. I really didn't like that the rules state that you add a random card from the draw deck to the cards players use to vote.
